species.name: Bramble Cay melomys
species.habitat: Herbaceous vegetation on a low coral cay.
species.threat_summary: Seawater inundation and vegetation loss support the climate link in this case.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: Elevation >15 m; 25–31 °C: do not use as proven tolerances.

species.name: Golden toad
species.habitat: Cloud forest and temporary breeding pools.
species.threat_summary: ENSO-related drought and disease have been proposed; attribution specifically to human-caused warming is disputed.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: 14–19 °C; RH >90 %: no tolerance source in the brief.

species.name: Chiriquí harlequin frog
species.threat_summary: The decline is attributed at least partly to chytridiomycosis; warming is not shown here to be the sole cause.

species.name: Southern gastric-brooding frog
species.habitat: Forest streams in the Conondale and Blackall ranges.
species.threat_summary: The causes were not resolved before it disappeared; disease is a leading hypothesis. Do not infer climate causation from these series.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: 15–20 °C water: not verified as a tolerance.

species.name: Northern Darwin’s frog
species.habitat: Native forest and streams; regional climate point, not a confirmed current population.
species.threat_summary: Not recorded since 1981. Habitat loss and disease need assessment; modern series alone cannot reconstruct its disappearance.

species.name: Oʻahu tree snail
species.status_basis: Hawaii DLNR, 2019; not an IUCN category
species.threat_summary: The last known individual died in captivity in 2019. Threats to Hawaiian snails include invasive species and climate; climate is not proven to be the sole cause for this species.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: 16–22 °C: no tolerance evidence in the brief.

species.name: Poʻouli
species.status_basis: USFWS, delisted due to extinction in 2023
species.threat_summary: Habitat loss, introduced species and disease all matter; the brief does not show that warming-driven malaria alone explains the extinction.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: 11–16 °C and >1500 m: do not treat as a guaranteed barrier against mosquitoes.

species.name: Tecopa pupfish
species.habitat: Outflows of two hot springs at Tecopa.
species.threat_summary: Modifying the springs for bathhouses altered flow and temperature; introduced fish are also considered. This is not evidence of extinction by global warming.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: 26–36 °C and never >40 °C: not adopted; the official report describes temperatures differently.

species.name: Millepora hydrocoral
species.habitat: Shallow reefs; distribution and taxonomy uncertain.
species.threat_summary: Severe declines and possible loss from Panama linked to ENSO; this is not global extinction. The latest assessment consulted is Data Deficient.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: 25–28 °C, anomalies >30 °C: not used as universal thresholds.

species.name: Galápagos damsel
species.status: Critically Endangered; possibly extinct in cited sources
species.habitat: Coastal waters, rocky shores and reef areas.
species.threat_summary: ENSO is linked to its apparent disappearance; status and evidence must distinguish possible from confirmed extinction.

species.name: Christmas Island forest skink
species.threat_summary: Confirmed extinction; predation by introduced species is relevant. Not attributed here to climate change. Replaces the brief row that mixed a pika and a rabbit.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: Pika/rabbit ranges are not transferred to this reptile.

species.name: Catarina pupfish
species.habitat: El Potosí spring and its aquatic surroundings.
species.threat_summary: Water extraction and habitat degradation are documented; the last captive fish died in 2014. Replaces the brief row that named no precise lake-fish species.
species.replacement_of: Cichlid / Chirostoma / Menidia; no defined species

species.name: Smooth handfish
species.habitat: Coastal marine setting of Tasmania; few records.
species.threat_summary: The 2020 Extinct listing was revised to Data Deficient. There is no basis to claim a confirmed climate extinction.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: 11–16 °C: no support as a biological limit.

species.name: Christmas Island pipistrelle
species.habitat: Rainforest, roost trees and insect-feeding areas.
species.threat_summary: The cause of decline is uncertain and multifactorial; invasive species and disturbance are key hypotheses. Do not present drought as a proven cause.

species.name: Rabbs’ fringe-limbed treefrog
species.habitat: Montane cloud forest; water-filled tree holes.
species.threat_summary: Decline and disease must be distinguished from causal attribution to warming. The death of the last known captive does not by itself make it Extinct.
species.pdf_threshold_claim: 18–23 °C: not validated as a survival limit.
